kept.spine: The town knows exactly what it could not survive, and that knowledge decides what it dares and what it lets go by.
The crisis at Warmholz has changed the posture and not the prospects. The town keeps the two apart on purpose.

kept.poolKey: Invasion & War: neither walls nor force
kept.spine: A traveller says nothing stands around the houses here, and at the first door he was asked only about the road behind him.
faces: A guard on the night round says he was given it street by street and left to guess at the rest.
At the tavern they give the reason there is no wall freely, and it comes out different at every table.
A clerk in the hall puts the want of a wall down to a want of money. He does not say what the money there is goes on.
The stallholders reckon the town's money here runs to the scales and the sweeping of the square.
A guild member says the trades could price a wall down to the carting. What they are asked for is money and never men.
Those who sit to hear a matter say nobody can put before them whether a line goes round the place, and they leave the question there.
The older heads here say the town has gotten by on being too small and too far from anywhere worth the trouble to need more than a barred door.
Whoever buries the dead says the ground for the dead is marked off and the rest of the place is not.

kept.spine: A dispute here is settled among the households themselves, and stays settled for only as long as everyone who was there keeps agreeing that it was.
faces: A pedlar says a shortfall in payment here is settled on the doorstep where it happened, and never travels past that door.
One of the elders says most matters are left for the households to settle themselves, and only what does not settle reaches the elders at all.
At the tavern they say the households which do the settling are the ones with the most fields, and the drinkers can name them.
The older heads here say a boundary in dispute is walked and argued over until both sides agree to it, and the walking falls to the two households, in time neither one can spare.
The muster says it is expected to stand behind whatever the households decide and is not asked first.
A quarrel that starts inside is none of the gate's, whoever keeps the gate says, and a quarrel that starts at the gate is settled at the gate.
Whoever digs the ground says they are told when to dig and not what was decided, and they do not ask.

kept.spine: What defending this place would cost, and whose cost it would be, has never been settled between the households.
faces: A drover says every household's store is kept under its own floor or in its own cellar, and the neighbours all know which floor covers what.
Those who keep the ground say a burying is the one thing here that waits for no purse.
A woman old enough to remember the custom says a household with nothing else to spare still finds what it takes to bury its own.
It is the same backs that come out, they say at the tavern. Everyone at the table can name the ones who stay behind their own door.
The muster says the ground it would gather on is somebody's own field, and that somebody would bear the trampling of the crop.
Those who hold the way through reckon nobody set the hour the bar comes down, and the hour follows the light.
The shortfall comes off the stalls, they say at the market, and the argument comes from behind every stall.
The soldiers say the place says plainly what it wants of them. The people here ask them straight out to put a shoulder to a load.

kept.poolKey: First-Survey qualification (the reading is a first look)
kept.spine: The safety reading for Warmholz is a first one. It is honest about what has been seen here and silent about what has not.
A stranger arrives at Warmholz from whichever direction suits him, and is not made to pass anybody on the way in.
No one at Warmholz can say whose task the town's defense is, and a stranger finds that out within an afternoon. It belongs to nobody in particular.
Nothing unseen has come at Warmholz, and nothing here would know if it had. Seeming safe and being able to tell are not the same thing.
This place is too small to wall, and it knows it. Its safety is its neighbours, its distance, and its unimportance.
The town holds no food buffer at all. Any break in what reaches it by road becomes a matter of days, not seasons.
